newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The prime minister has chosen the president of Thai Military Bank as finance minister after Olarn Chaipravat, the first choice candidate, turned down his offer. Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says Thanong Bidaya has accepted the position and is returning from Hong Kong to be back in time for royal appointment. (BANGKOK POST)

- A judicial probe team has recommended the dismissal with pension of a senior judge who granted bail to Li Yun Chung. In a 28-page summary of the investigation report, the panel gives its recommendation that Somchai Udomwong's action to grant bail to the drug suspect tarnished the judicial system. It suggests he be dismissed from government service to avoid damage to the state. (BANGKOK POST)

- A recent university poll shows that 80 percent of respondents believe people convicted of serious crimes should face the death penalty, reasoning this would help decrease the growing number of crimes. Supong Limtanakul, deputy dean of Bangkok University, says 82.3 percent of 2,500 respondents believe that capital punishment will serve to reduce the number of serious crimes, while 17.7 percent disagree. (THE NATION)

- The Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) has reached agreement with the Lao government for the purchase of 700 MW of electricity from the hydro-power projects Nam Ngum 2 and 3. EGAT and the Lao government will sign a memorandum of understanding in Laos during August. (BUSINESS DAY)
